subject.title: [Feature]: Global (IP-agnostic) auth rate limiting option for public-exposed deployments

question: Should Gateway auth support an opt-in IP-agnostic failed-auth lockout mode for public password/token deployments, despite the intentional all-client lockout tradeoff?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but the permanent behavior changes an authentication security boundary and creates a deliberate availability failure mode under attack, so maintainer/security intent is required.

options.title: Add default-off global mode
options.body: Implement gateway.auth.rateLimit.global as an explicit operator-controlled mode with docs and tests while preserving the current per-IP default.

options.title: Keep mitigation outside core
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core per-IP only and recommend identity-aware proxies or external controls for public deployments.

options.title: Defer to broader Gateway hardening
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers settle a wider public-exposure hardening plan covering password strength, lockout semantics, and rate-limit policy.

recommendation.title: Add default-off global mode
recommendation.body: Implement gateway.auth.rateLimit.global as an explicit operator-controlled mode with docs and tests while preserving the current per-IP default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the original Gateway auth limiter and is the clearest individual routing signal alongside required secops review.
